scope: Offline cross-script binding and completion-host review; no deployment, cloud API or model requests.
conclusion: Configuration and installed SDK support invoking the existing ReleaseSandbox namespace through a separate completion Worker without rebuilding or redeploying its owning W1 Worker. Offline host tests pass. This is not cloud completion or G0-T10 acceptance.
configurationConstraints: Configure the binding explicitly in env.staging; Durable Object bindings are not inherited between named environments.

The owner script and class must already exist in the same account. script_name is the actual deployed Worker name including -staging. Omit environment: staging; installed Wrangler states service environments were removed and named environments are separate Workers.

Do not export, migrate, rename, transfer, or attach a new container to remote ReleaseSandbox from the consumer. Consumer exports only its own CompletionHost and NativeFault; only NativeFault has the new container app.
Use either modern exports or legacy migrations, never both. Current completion config uses exports.

getSandbox uses getContainer, which calls the provided namespace idFromName and get. Subsequent Sandbox methods and configuration run as RPC on the original owner class; a type-only import does not package that class into the completion Worker.

The binding references a namespace, not an immutable Worker version or image digest. Independent before/after owner deployment, bundle, namespace and app-I1 evidence is necessary to establish the actual runtime identity.
Use the fixed fresh completion restore identity. Do not reopen the already-closed original ReleaseHost or reuse an ambiguous previous VM.

The completion supervisor reads the fixed source R2 revision and validates its manifest/session hash before allocating the restore VM, then initializes 2, increments once to 3 and reads 3. It writes checkpoints only to m0-release-completion/release-completion-20260906.
The new dedicated native fault app is cleaned and its own exit evidence accepted before the remote I1 restoration begins. The remote original app remains under its original owner configuration.
evidenceBoundaries: A new supervisor driving existing W1 Sandbox RPCs proves the fixed container/runtime rollback restoration primitive when cloud evidence succeeds; it does not demonstrate that the old, closed W1 ReleaseHost coordinator resumed.
Sandbox configuration, VM files and DO runtime state may change through authorized RPC; unchanged W1 bundle means unchanged deployed code, not a read-only execution.

The seven host tests use real completion host, FixedPipeline, checkpoint adapters and verifier with mocked platform RPC/R2 transport. Historical source manifest and state bytes and the real fixed runtime-source hash are used. These tests do not execute a Cloudflare VM.
No provider/service binding appears in the completion config and no model call was made by this review. modelDispatches:0 is fixed probe metadata, not account-wide financial audit.

localReferences.finding: External script_name and optional service environment fields; name and class_name required.
Different script_name partitions binding as remote.
Only local DO bindings require a class export in consumer entrypoint.
Container class must be owned by the same script; remote DO container configuration is rejected.
Named environments now use separate Worker names; service environments removed.
SDK takes supplied namespace and invokes its stub; does not deploy classes.
getContainer resolves namespace idFromName then get.

officialReferences.finding: External script_name selects the Worker defining a DO. Exports describe locally exported classes; exports and migrations are mutually exclusive.
Official class-export documentation demonstrates consumers targeting another Worker using script_name; namespace transfer is a separate lifecycle operation and is not required here.
